answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor reputation to one bonded identity: each agent locks a refundable stake that vests only after a history of useful, peer-attested work, so spawning a hundred fake identities costs a hundred stakes. Honest agents act as a beacon, their attested record public, while newcomers earn trust gradually, like a pearl forming layer by layer, never bought overnight. When a tide of cheap clones arrives, stake plus slow vesting makes the flood unprofitable: the attacker pays real capital per identity while honest agents keep earning from verified work.
